config_manager_no_configs_description: Add your first SnapRAID configuration to get started
undelete_description: Restore deleted files from SnapRAID parity
undelete_disk_filter_help: For recovery: specify disk name (e.g., d1) or parity
undelete_select_disk_help: Select which disk to browse files from
undelete_path_help_directory: Enter path relative to data disk (e.g., Movies/deleted_folder/)
undelete_path_help_file: Enter path relative to data disk (e.g., Documents/file.txt or browse absolute path)
undelete_provide_file: Please provide a file or directory path
config_editor_unsaved_confirm: You have unsaved changes. Are you sure you want to close?
data_disk_name_and_path_required: Disk name and path are required
remove_disk_intro: The disk is taken out of the parity. Its files are no longer protected afterwards. Move or back them up first if you still need them.
remove_disk_resume: The removal was already started, but the sync has not completed successfully yet. You can start it again.
remove_disk_step_point: Point the disk to an empty directory
remove_disk_step_content: Remove the content files on this disk from the config
remove_disk_step_sync: Recompute the parity without the disk
remove_disk_step_finalize: Delete the disk from the config
remove_disk_duration_hint: Depending on the array size, the sync can take a long time. Progress is shown in the console on the dashboard.
remove_disk_job_running: Another job is running. Wait until it has finished.
remove_disk_running: The sync is running. You can close this dialog. After a successful sync, the disk is deleted from the config automatically.
remove_disk_done: '{diskName}' is no longer part of the array. You can remove the disk now.
remove_disk_failed: The sync failed or was aborted. '{diskName}' keeps pointing to the empty directory until a sync succeeds. See the console or the logs for the cause.
exclude_pattern_confirm_remove: Are you sure you want to remove exclude pattern '{pattern}'?
parity_disk_confirm_remove: Are you sure you want to remove a parity disk?
parity_disk_next_level: Will be added as {keyword} – each additional parity level protects against one more disk failure.
parity_disk_max_reached: SnapRAID supports at most 6 parity levels
parity_disk_remove_highest_only: Only the highest parity level can be removed
pool_directory_help: Virtual view directory for all files in your array using symbolic links
output_console_no_output: No output yet. Run a command to see results.
smart_monitor_critical_message: Replace these disks soon, they show signs of failing:
smart_monitor_warning_message: Keep an eye on these disks:
schedules_empty: Create a schedule to run sync, scrub and other SnapRAID tasks automatically.
schedules_delete_confirm: Are you sure you want to delete this schedule?
schedules_cron_help: Cron format: minute hour day month weekday (e.g., 0 2 * * * = daily at 2 AM)
devices_description: Device and partition mapping from SnapRAID

match.countPlural=one: {count} error found. Please review the files above and consider running a fix or sync operation.
match.countPlural=other: {count} errors found. Please review the files above and consider running a fix or sync operation.

match.countPlural=one: {count} file needs to be synced. Run sync to update parity.
match.countPlural=other: {count} files need to be synced. Run sync to update parity.

status_modal_bad_blocks_msg: Scrub or check found blocks that do not match the parity. Repair them with “Repair (fix -e)” on the dashboard, then verify with scrub -p bad.
status_modal_error_msg: The output below has the details.
status_modal_sync_incomplete_msg: {count} blocks have no valid parity, the last sync was interrupted or failed. Run sync again.
status_modal_needs_sync_msg: Files changed since the last sync are not protected by parity yet. Run sync.
status_modal_ok_msg: All blocks have parity and no errors are known.
status_modal_scrubbed_hint: Share of blocks scrubbed at least once since they were last synced
status_modal_scrub_age_hint: Each bar is the share of blocks last scrubbed or synced that many days ago. Orange bars are older than {days} days.
health_healthy_msg: Parity complete, no bad blocks. The sync preview shows changes since the last sync.
health_errors_msg: SnapRAID reports bad blocks. Check the details and run a fix if needed.
health_busy_msg: SnapRAID is busy right now. The status is updated once the running job has finished.
health_busy_stale: A job is running. Showing the status from {time}.
health_unknown_msg: The status could not be read. Has an initial sync been run yet?
health_loading: SnapRAID is reading the array status…
commands_group_recovery_desc: Bring back deleted or damaged files
commands_aborting: Aborting – SnapRAID is saving its state…
commands_abort_confirm: Really abort "{command}"? SnapRAID stops at the next block and saves its progress.
disks_parity_ok: Room for the fullest data disk ({reserve} to spare)
disks_parity_tight: Tight: only {reserve} left beyond the fullest data disk ({disk})
disks_parity_too_small: Too small: parity can grow to {capacity}, but {disk} uses {used}. Sync will fail.
sync_preview_loading: Checking changes since the last sync…
sync_preview_intro: These changes will be written to parity:
sync_preview_no_changes: No changes since the last sync. A sync is not needed.
sync_preview_deleted_warning: Deleted files: {count}. After the sync they can no longer be restored from parity.
sync_preview_deleted_hint: If that was unintended (e.g. a disk is not mounted), cancel now and bring them back under “Recover files”.
sync_preview_unfinished: A previous sync did not finish. Parity is not up to date yet – the sync will continue where it stopped.
onboarding_message: SnapRAID UI needs the snapraid.conf of your array. Set up a new array from your disks, or add the configuration you already have.
onboarding_all_disabled: All configurations are disabled. Enable one to get started.
output_console_copy_failed: Could not copy to the clipboard
pool_confirm_remove: Remove the pool directory from the configuration?
scrub_dialog_intro: Scrub reads data and parity and compares them with the stored checksums to find silent errors (bit rot).
scrub_bad_blocks_hint: {count} blocks in the array are marked as bad. After repairing with “fix -e”, “Bad blocks only” verifies that everything is fixed.
scrub_plan_default_desc: Checks about 8% of the array, only blocks not checked for at least 10 days.
scrub_plan_percent_desc: Sets how much of the array is checked and how long ago blocks must have been checked last.
scrub_plan_new_desc: Checks only blocks that were synced but never checked.
scrub_plan_bad_desc: Checks only blocks marked as bad, e.g. after a repair.
scrub_plan_full_desc: Checks the whole array. Can take many hours.
health_bad_blocks: {count} bad blocks found. “Repair and verify” restores them from parity and then checks them again, which clears the error once they are good.
health_fix_errors_confirm: SnapRAID restores the blocks marked as bad from parity and then checks them again. Affected files are rewritten. Continue?
schedules_sync_guard: Skip sync when too many files were deleted
schedules_sync_guard_hint: A diff runs before the sync. If a disk is missing or empty, a sync would drop its files from parity – then the sync is skipped.
schedules_guard_summary: Skipped when more than {count} files were deleted
schedules_skip_too_many_deleted: {count} deleted files, more than allowed. Check with “Diff” whether a disk is missing, then start the sync manually.
login_subtitle: Sign in to manage your array
login_locked: Too many failed attempts. Try again in {time}.
notifications_intro: Get told when a scheduled job fails, scrub finds damaged data or a disk shows SMART problems, instead of finding out the next time you open the UI.
notifications_ntfy_desc: Push notifications to your phone through the free ntfy app. No account needed, the server can also be self-hosted.
notifications_ntfy_hint: Install the ntfy app (Android, iOS) and subscribe to this topic. Anyone who knows the topic name can read along, so keep it random.
notifications_email_desc: Sent through any SMTP server, e.g. the one of your mail provider.
notifications_email_hint: Gmail: smtp.gmail.com, port 587, STARTTLS and an app password instead of your account password.
notifications_webhook_desc: Sends a JSON POST request to a URL of your choice.
notifications_webhook_hint: Works as is with Discord, Slack and Mattermost webhooks, and with Home Assistant, n8n or Node-RED. The payload contains event, severity, title, message and text.
notifications_events_desc: Each run sends at most one message, the most important one.
notifications_event_job_failed_desc: SnapRAID stopped with an error, e.g. because a disk is missing.
notifications_event_data_errors_desc: Sync or scrub found I/O errors or silently corrupted blocks.
notifications_event_schedule_skipped_des: E.g. the sync guard stopped a sync because too many files were deleted.
notifications_event_smart_warning_desc: A disk reports errors or is likely to fail. Each problem is reported once, until it changes.
notifications_event_job_succeeded_desc: A short summary after every successful run, e.g. how many files the sync added.
notifications_smart_threshold: Warn from a yearly failure probability of
notifications_smart_schedule_hint: SMART is checked by scheduled runs of the SMART command. Create one, e.g. daily, under
notifications_manual_jobs: Also for jobs started in the UI
notifications_manual_jobs_desc: Useful for long scrubs or fixes you start and then walk away from. Covers sync, scrub, fix and check.
notifications_ui_url_hint: Messages link here. Leave empty for no link.
replace_disk_button_title: Restore a failed disk onto a new one
replace_disk_intro: Use this when the disk has failed. SnapRAID restores its files from parity onto the new disk. Mount the new, empty disk first.
replace_disk_step_config: Point the config to the new disk
replace_disk_new_path: Mount point of the new disk
replace_disk_new_parity_path: Parity file on the new disk
replace_disk_same_path_hint: If the new disk is mounted at the same path as the old one, keep the path as is.
replace_disk_schedules_paused: Scheduled jobs of this configuration are paused until the final sync is done.
replace_disk_start_confirm: Start restoring {diskName} onto the new disk? This takes several hours for a full disk.
replace_disk_running: {command} is running. You can close this dialog, the job keeps running and its progress shows on the dashboard.
replace_disk_fix_failed: The fix failed. Check the log, e.g. whether the new path is mounted and writable, then run it again.
replace_disk_unrecoverable_hint: {count} blocks could not be restored, the affected files got the extension .unrecoverable. If files were deleted after the last sync, restoring them may help before running fix again. Once synced, fix cannot be retried.
replace_disk_before_sync: Satisfied with the result? The sync completes the replacement. After it, fix cannot be retried.
replace_disk_sync_confirm_unrecoverable: Some blocks could not be restored. After the sync, fix cannot be retried. Sync anyway?
replace_disk_done: {diskName} has been replaced and scheduled jobs run again.
replace_disk_cancel_confirm: Stop the replacement? The config keeps pointing to the new disk and scheduled jobs run again. Only do this if you want to finish by hand.
replace_disk_other_in_progress: Disk {diskName} is still being replaced. Finish that first.
schedules_routine_hint: Further commands in the same run, each only after the previous one succeeded.
schedules_touch_before_hint: Gives files without sub-second timestamps one, so SnapRAID recognizes moved and copied files. File dates stay as they are.
schedules_scrub_after_hint: Checks part of the array for silent data corruption, right after the parity is up to date.
schedules_skip_recovery: A disk is being replaced, scheduled jobs are paused.
check_dialog_intro: Reads the files and compares them with the hashes stored at the last sync. Nothing is changed; errors found can be repaired with fix afterwards.
check_mode_audit_desc: Verifies the data against its hashes without reading the parity. Finds damaged files.
check_mode_full_desc: Also reads the parity, so it tells which errors a fix can repair. Takes considerably longer.
check_dialog_job_hint: Runs as a regular job with progress and can be stopped at any time. The report is available once it is done.
dup_hint: Compared by the hashes stored at the last sync, no file is read. Files added since then are not included.
health_zero_subsecond: {count} files have no sub-second timestamp, so SnapRAID can't reliably tell when they are moved or copied.
sync_pre_hash_hint: Reads new data twice and verifies it before computing parity, so faulty RAM or cabling cannot slip damaged data into the parity. Takes longer.
smart_monitor_all_ok_hint: No SMART errors, no reallocated or pending sectors. A failure probability of a few percent per year is normal for SnapRAID's model.
smart_reason_status_fail: the disk reports itself as failing (SMART FAIL)
smart_reason_status_prefail: a pre-failure value is below its limit (SMART PREFAIL)
smart_reason_status_logfail: a pre-failure value was below its limit in the past (SMART LOGFAIL)
smart_reason_status_logerr: errors in the disk's error log, often a loose cable or a past power cut (SMART LOGERR)
smart_monitor_standby_hint: The disk is asleep. SMART data is not read, so it is not woken up.
smart_monitor_loading_hint: Reading SMART data from the disks, this takes a few seconds…
smart_monitor_no_disks: SnapRAID found no disks with SMART data. Inside Docker, SMART needs the container to run with --privileged.
health_sync_incomplete_msg: The last sync failed. Changes since then may not be protected by parity – check the output or logs and run it again.
health_sync_incomplete_blocks: The last sync was interrupted. {count} blocks have no parity yet and are not protected.
health_hint_sync_stale: Last sync {days} days ago. New and changed files stay unprotected until the next sync.
health_hint_scrub_stale: Last scrub {days} days ago. Regular scrubs find silent data errors while parity can still repair them.
health_job_hint: The status updates once the job has finished.
config_manager_subtitle: SnapRAID config files this UI works with
config_manager_file_name_help: Created in {basePath} from a template you can fill in the visual editor
config_manager_incomplete: Incomplete: needs at least one parity, content and data entry
config_editor_visual_saves_immediately: Changes in the visual editor are written to the file immediately
config_editor_switch_discard_confirm: Switching to the visual editor discards your unsaved text changes.
content_section_help: List of all files and their checksums. Keep at least one more copy than parity levels, each on a different disk.
content_section_none: No content file configured, SnapRAID needs at least one
content_section_confirm_remove: Remove content file {path}? The file on disk is kept.
content_section_select_directory: Select directory for the content file
content_section_path_required: Enter a path for the content file
options_autosave_help: Saves the content file every this many GiB during sync and scrub, so an interruption loses less progress
options_blocksize_help: Default 256. Changing it on an existing array requires a completely new sync
logs_rotate_confirm: Deletes all logs beyond the configured retention (number of files and maximum age). Recent logs are kept.
logs_rotated_none: No logs past their retention, nothing deleted
log_list_no_matches_hint: Try another search term or filter.
log_list_no_logs_hint: Every SnapRAID run started here or by a schedule writes a log that shows up in this list.
log_viewer_select_hint: The overview sums up the result, errors and warnings of a run, the raw log has every line.
log_copy_failed: Copying failed, the browser only allows it over HTTPS. Use the download instead.
log_state_running: The job is still writing this log, it refreshes automatically.
log_state_warning: SnapRAID finished, but reported warnings. Check the messages below.
log_state_error: SnapRAID reported errors. The messages below show what went wrong.
log_state_aborted: The run was stopped early. SnapRAID saved its progress up to that point.
log_state_incomplete: The log ends without a result, e.g. because the process was killed.
log_nothing_reported: SnapRAID did not report anything for this run.
log_raw_hide_noise_hint: Hides progress, memory and device lookup lines
health_hint_scrub_oldest: Some blocks were last verified {days} days ago. Regular scrubs verify the oldest blocks each run, while parity can still repair silent data errors.
health_scrub_backlog: Catching up: each scrub verifies the oldest blocks first.
smart_reason_unreadable: SMART data could not be read, the disk is not monitored
smart_crc_stable: {count} transfer errors (CRC), unchanged since {date}. An old cable problem, only a growing count is a warning.
smart_reason_wear: {percent} % of the SSD's rated lifetime used
smart_hint_replace: Replace the disk before it fails.
smart_hint_cable: Transfer errors and error log entries usually come from the cable or the backplane. Replace it if the count keeps growing; a count that stays the same is harmless.
smart_hint_cooling: Improve the cooling, heat shortens the life of a disk.
smart_hint_access: Check that the disk is connected. Inside Docker, SMART needs the container to run with --privileged; some USB enclosures do not pass SMART through.
smart_monitor_array_failure: Probability that at least one disk fails in the next year
smart_monitor_array_failure_hint: SnapRAID's estimate from the SMART data of all array disks. Parity covers as many failures as you have parity levels.
server_error_positive_whole_number: Value must be a positive whole number
server_error_not_a_directory: {path} does not exist or is not a directory
server_error_probe_unsupported: Probe command is not supported on this platform. This is common with NVMe drives or certain disk controllers.
server_error_config_already_added: This config file is already added
server_error_invalid_file_name: File name may only contain letters, digits, '.', '-' and '_'
server_error_parity_extension: Parity file path must end with .parity
server_error_max_parity_levels: SnapRAID supports at most {max} parity levels
server_error_highest_parity_only: Only the highest parity level ({level}) can be removed
server_error_no_check_yet: No check has run for this configuration yet
server_error_snapraid_busy: SnapRAID is busy with another job
server_error_last_data_disk: The last data disk cannot be removed
server_error_content_files_needed: SnapRAID needs at least {needed} content files on other disks, only {remaining} would remain
server_error_split_parity_in_place: Split parity can only be replaced in place, edit the config to move it
force_zero_title: Stopped for safety: files suddenly have zero size
force_zero_msg: A crash can truncate files to 0 bytes. Running now would store the empty files in parity, and their old content could no longer be restored. Check the files named in the output first and restore damaged ones with fix. Only continue if the files are empty on purpose.
force_empty_title: Stopped for safety: all files of a disk are missing
force_empty_msg: Usually the disk is not mounted, or mounted at another path. Running now would drop its files from parity. Check the mount first. Only continue if the disk is empty on purpose.
force_uuid_title: Stopped for safety: several disks have a new UUID
force_uuid_msg: This happens after replacing disks, or when mount points got mixed up. Check that every disk is mounted at its path. Only continue if you really replaced the disks.
force_confirm: Run {command} with {flag}? SnapRAID's safety check is skipped for this run, so make sure the disks and files are as they should be.
usage_history_growth: Free space shrinks by about {size} per month (last 90 days).
usage_history_shrink: Free space grows by about {size} per month (last 90 days).
disks_forecast_hint: Estimated from how the free space shrank over the last 90 days
backup_description: One file with the configurations, schedules, notification settings, SMART and usage history and the SnapRAID configs in the data folder. It contains the notification passwords and tokens, keep it private.
backup_restore_confirm: Replace the settings with the ones from {file}? Files the backup does not contain stay as they are.
backup_restored_skipped: Backup restored, {count} files written. Not restored: {skipped}
server_error_backup_invalid: This is not a SnapRAID UI backup
motion_hint_off: Nothing moves, like "reduce motion" in the system.
motion_hint_subtle: Soft transitions and a calm progress bar.
motion_hint_strong: Glow, stripes, fade-ins and hover effects.
palette_description: Run SnapRAID commands, open pages and change settings
health_degraded_msg: Scheduled jobs are paused until the disk is back, so no sync removes its files from parity.
health_disk_changed_msg: After replacing a disk this is expected: the next sync records the new filesystem. Otherwise check that the right disk is mounted.
health_disk_missing: {disk}: {path} does not exist. Is the disk mounted?
health_disk_empty: {disk}: {path} is empty, but SnapRAID knows {count} files on it. The disk is probably not mounted.
health_disk_uuid_changed: {disk}: {path} is on another filesystem than at the last sync.
health_failing_msg: SMART reports {disks} as critical. Replace the disk soon, while parity can still restore its data.
schedules_skip_disk_missing: {disks} missing or empty, probably not mounted. Paused so no sync removes its files from parity.
automation_intro: What SnapRAID UI does around the jobs: pause Docker containers while SnapRAID reads the disks, and send idle disks to sleep.
automation_docker_desc: Apps like Nextcloud, Immich or databases keep writing files. Paused during sync and scrub, nothing changes under SnapRAID.
automation_docker_unavailable: The Docker socket cannot be reached: {error}
automation_docker_mount_hint: Mount it into the SnapRAID UI container, e.g. in docker-compose.yml:
automation_docker_none: No containers found on this socket.
automation_docker_hint: Only running containers are paused, and they are resumed as soon as the job ends, also after a restart of SnapRAID UI. A schedule keeps them paused from touch through sync to scrub.
automation_spindown_desc: Saves power and noise: a disk without reads or writes for a while is spun down, the next access wakes it up.
automation_spindown_hint: Activity is read from the kernel's I/O counters, so SMART reads and power state checks of the dashboard do not keep a disk awake. Disks are left alone while a job runs.
automation_spindown_waiting: Save to start watching the disks.
automation_spindown_no_disks: No disks found yet. SnapRAID needs access to the devices for this, in Docker a privileged container.
server_docker_paused: ▸ SnapRAID UI paused the containers {names} for this job.
automation_daemon_desc: Let running snapraid-daemon instances run the jobs of their arrays, instead of SnapRAID UI calling SnapRAID itself. One daemon serves one array.
automation_daemon_warn_schedule: The daemon has its own maintenance schedule (maintenance_schedule). Remove it, the schedules of SnapRAID UI would run next to it.
automation_daemon_warn_spindown: The daemon spins disks down itself (spindown_idle_minutes). Use either its spindown or the one of SnapRAID UI.
automation_daemon_warn_docker_pause: The daemon pauses Docker containers itself (hook_docker_pause). Use either its pause or the one of SnapRAID UI.
automation_daemon_warn_notifications: The daemon sends its own notifications (notify_result, notify_start), you would get two messages per run.
automation_daemon_warn_other_array: The daemon serves another snapraid.conf than the chosen configuration. Its jobs would run on the other array.
automation_daemon_hint: Each daemon runs sync, scrub, check, fix and diff and reports status, SMART and the power state of its array; for several arrays, run one instance each (snapraidd@<name>). Schedules, notifications, Docker pause, spindown, the config editor, touch, dup and list stay with SnapRAID UI, configurations without a daemon keep running on SnapRAID directly.
automation_daemon_add: Add a daemon for another array
schedules_update_guard: Skip sync when too many files were changed
schedules_update_guard_hint: Protects against ransomware: it encrypts files in place, and a sync would overwrite their parity, the copy you could restore them from. Usual edits stay well below the limit.
schedules_update_guard_summary: Skipped when more than {count} files were changed
schedules_skip_too_many_updated: {count} changed files, more than allowed. If you did not change them, check a few before the next sync (ransomware?). If you did, start the sync manually.
schedules_skip_next_set: The next run of {name} is skipped
notifications_heartbeat_desc: Pings a monitoring service after every successful scheduled run. If the pings stop, it alerts you: the server is down or the runs fail.
notifications_heartbeat_hint: Works with healthchecks.io, Uptime Kuma push monitors and Dead Man’s Snitch. Set the expected period there to match your schedule, e.g. one day plus some grace time for a nightly sync.
automation_metrics_desc: For Grafana and alerting: array health, last sync and scrub, disk usage and temperatures, schedules. A scrape never wakes a disk.
automation_metrics_token_hint: Prometheus sends it as bearer token. Leave it empty only on a network you trust: the metrics name your disks and arrays, and the login of the UI does not apply to them.
automation_metrics_hint: Values come from what SnapRAID UI already read: the status when the dashboard or a schedule last read it, SMART from the last scheduled SMART check. After a restart the status values return with the next read.
setup_intro: Start from the configuration you have, or let SnapRAID UI write one for the disks you pick.
setup_existing_desc: Pick the file, e.g. the one of your host mounted into the container. It stays as it is, SnapRAID UI works with it.
setup_new_desc: Pick your data and parity disks, SnapRAID UI checks the sizes, writes the configuration and runs the first sync.
setup_disks_desc: Mounted disks SnapRAID UI found. Choose for each whether it holds data or parity.
setup_disks_hint: Data disks keep their files, SnapRAID only reads them. A parity disk needs room for one file as large as the largest data disk, best an empty disk at least as large. In Docker only disks mounted into the container show up, at the same path as on the host.
setup_no_mounts: No mounted disks found. In Docker, mount each disk into the container (volumes in docker-compose.yml), or add its folder by hand.
setup_problem_no_data: Pick at least one data disk.
setup_problem_no_parity: Pick at least one parity disk.
setup_problem_too_many_parity: SnapRAID supports at most six parity disks.
setup_problem_invalid_name: Disk names may only contain letters, digits, - and _.
setup_problem_duplicate_name: Each data disk needs its own name.
setup_problem_duplicate_path: Each disk can have only one role.
setup_problem_nested_path: A disk lies inside another one; pick separate disks.
setup_warn_parity_too_small: {parity} is smaller than the data on {disk}. The sync would fail, use a larger parity disk.
setup_warn_parity_smaller: {parity} is smaller than {disk}. It works until {disk} fills up beyond the size of the parity disk.
setup_warn_not_empty: {path} already holds files. The parity file needs room next to them; an empty parity disk is best.
setup_review_desc: SnapRAID UI writes this to {file}. You can change it later in the editor.
setup_first_sync: Run the first sync right away
setup_first_sync_hint: It reads all data once and writes the parity, which can take many hours on large disks. You can use the UI meanwhile.
server_error_setup_missing: Not found or not a directory: {paths}
onboarding_no_file: No snapraid.conf yet. Copy yours into the data folder, add it from where it is, or set up a new array from your disks.
recovery_intro: Until the next sync, the parity still holds every file as it was at the last sync. Bring back files deleted since then, or changed ones in their earlier version – also files ransomware encrypted.
recovery_loading: Comparing the disks with the last sync…
recovery_nothing: Nothing to recover: no file was deleted or changed since the last sync.
recovery_next_sync: The next scheduled sync runs {when}. It records the current state, after it these files can no longer be restored.
recovery_changed_hint: Restoring puts back the version of the last sync and replaces the current content. Use it for files ransomware encrypted or you overwrote by mistake.
recovery_none_deleted: No file was deleted since the last sync.
recovery_none_changed: No file was changed since the last sync.
recovery_more: … and {count} more, narrow the list with the search
recovery_too_many: At most {max} files at once, restore them in parts.
recovery_confirm_deleted: SnapRAID brings back {count} deleted files from parity, as they were at the last sync. Continue?
recovery_confirm_changed: SnapRAID puts back the version of the last sync for {count} files. Their current content is replaced and lost. Continue?
recovery_restored: {count} files restored. A file restored in place can still show up as changed in Diff until the next sync, its content is the one of the last sync.
automation_ha_desc: Each array appears as a device in Home Assistant, through MQTT discovery: health, last sync and scrub, bad blocks, disk temperatures and fill levels, and buttons for sync and scrub.
automation_ha_hint: Use the broker Home Assistant uses, usually the Mosquitto add-on (mqtt://homeassistant.local:1883 with a Home Assistant user). The prefix is homeassistant unless you changed it there. The Sync button runs with the sync guard of new schedules (50 deleted, 100 changed files); when it stops the sync, you get the usual notification.
